objective.primary_metric: matched fixed-90 end-to-end tokens/sec, maximize subject to exact output gate

hypothesis: An intermediate three-layer draft may preserve the five-layer acceptance gain with less draft latency.
kill_criterion: Reject promotion if exact output gate fails or matched end-to-end throughput does not beat the one-layer incumbent.

effective_execution.backend_or_kernel: existing official DFlash2 modules plus SmolLM compatibility bridge and exact singleton guard

result.correctness: 180/180 target-equivalent timed outputs for both models
result.memory: 3-layer peak 354971648 bytes; RTX 3060 remained within gate

learning.what_worked: Identity-initialized intermediate expansion preserved exact logits against its actual two-layer parent, and the candidate passed the full fixed-90 exact guard.
learning.what_failed: Three-layer capacity improved acceptance but did not overcome added draft latency; CE training overfit after epoch 0.
learning.causal_interpretation: observed acceptance and throughput tradeoff; the reason added capacity does not pay for itself beyond draft compute is inferred, not isolated.
learning.reusable_lesson: Intermediate depth should be rejected as a serving candidate unless it beats the current throughput incumbent under the same exact contract.
learning.next_hypothesis: Prioritize acceptance-calibrated objective or verifier/runtime fidelity over blind depth scaling.
